transcript.text: Every so often when I put the washing machine on the whole kitchen power goes off and I have to go to the fuse box and flick the switch back up. It doesn't happen every time. Indesit, IWE 7 something.

This is very common with washing machines, and it's usually a fault in the machine rather than your wiring. The fact that it's intermittent is a useful clue.

## First: which switch is tripping?

Look at the switch you flick back up:

• RCD (usually wider, has a "T" or "Test" button, often labelled RCD and covering several circuits). It trips when electricity leaks to earth. This is the most likely culprit with a washing machine.
• MCB (narrow switch for one circuit, labelled e.g. "Kitchen" or "Sockets"). It trips from overload or a short.

## If it's the RCD (most likely)

Something in the machine is leaking a small amount of current to earth. Notice when in the cycle it trips, because that points to the cause:

| When it trips | Likely cause |
|---|---|
| A few minutes in, once it's filled and starts heating | Heating element (by far the most common cause, especially on hot washes) |
| Only on hot/long washes, not quick cold ones | Heating element again, which explains the "not every time" |
| During spin | Motor (worn brushes, damp or dirty motor) |
| When draining | Drain pump |
| The moment you switch it on | Mains filter/suppressor or a damp plug or socket |
| Random, maybe after a leak | Water dripping onto wiring inside |

Also, an RCD trips at a total leakage threshold, so a slightly leaky washer plus a fridge or dishwasher on the same circuit can tip it over.

## If it's the MCB

• Is the kettle, dishwasher, oven, or tumble dryer often on at the same time? That could be overload. Try running the washer alone.
• If it trips even when running alone, there's likely a short in the machine, plug, or socket.

## Things you can check safely

1. Unplug the machine and check the plug and socket for scorch marks, melting, or a burning smell. If you find any, stop using that socket and call an electrician.
2. Look underneath and behind for signs of water leaks or dampness.
3. Try a cold, short wash. If it never trips on that but does on 40°C+, the heating element is the prime suspect.
4. Don't use an extension lead as a workaround.

## Fixing it

• A heating element for an Indesit IWE7 is usually a cheap part (around £20–40). It's a moderately easy DIY job if you're handy, but an appliance repair engineer can confirm it in minutes with an insulation tester, so you don't replace the wrong part.
• If the machine is old (over 10 years) and needs a motor, a new machine may be better value.

## Safety note

An RCD tripping is it doing its job and protecting you from shock. Resetting it occasionally is fine, but don't keep running a machine that regularly trips it. And if it starts tripping with the washer unplugged, the problem is elsewhere, and you should get an electrician in.

If you can tell me which switch trips and roughly when in the cycle, I can narrow it down further.

Thanks, that's helpful. I've been keeping notes, so here is what I have. It's the wide switch at the fuse box that trips, the one for the kitchen sockets, not the individual little breaker. It happens roughly 1 in 4 washes over the last month, always a few minutes into a 40 or 60 degree wash, and never on a cold wash, quick 30, or rinse and spin. It has tripped with the kettle and dishwasher off, and I tried the hall socket once and it tripped that one too. The plug looks fine, not warm and no marks, and I haven't smelled burning or seen any sparks. I have been resetting it each time, though.

Your notes point clearly to one culprit: the heating element.

## Why the heating element

• The wide switch is the RCD, so it's earth leakage, not overload.
• It only trips on 40°C and 60°C washes, a few minutes in. That's exactly when the machine finishes filling and switches the heater on.
• It never trips on cold, quick 30, or rinse and spin. Those cycles don't use the heater, or barely do.
• It trips intermittently (about 1 in 4). This is typical of an element starting to break down. The insulation inside leaks only when hot or under certain conditions.
• It tripped with other appliances off and on a different socket. That rules out overload and your kitchen socket or wiring.

Elements fail like this through age and limescale. The metal sheath cracks or the insulation degrades, so a little current leaks to earth through the water and the machine's casing.

## Is it safe to keep resetting?

The RCD is doing its job, cutting the power quickly when it detects leakage, so resetting it hasn't been dangerous in itself. But:

• Stick to cold or quick 30 washes until it's fixed. Those don't use the element.
• Elements usually get worse, not better, so the trips will likely become more frequent.
• If it starts tripping on cold washes too, or the RCD won't reset, unplug the machine and stop using it until it's checked.

## Getting it fixed

Option 1: Engineer or appliance repairer
• The most straightforward option. They can confirm it with an insulation resistance tester, which is the proper test. A normal multimeter often misses this kind of fault.
• Expect roughly £80–150 all in, depending on your area.

Option 2: DIY replacement (if you're reasonably handy)
• Find the exact model number on the sticker inside the door rim or on the back. "IWE 7..." covers several variants.
• Elements for these are typically £15–35 online.
• Unplug the machine first and turn off the water.
• Remove the relevant panel (on most Indesit IWE models it's the back panel, but check for your model), disconnect the wires, loosen the central nut, and ease the element out. There are plenty of model-specific videos online.
• Make sure the new one seats properly into its bracket inside the drum. A misaligned element can damage the drum.

Is it worth fixing? An element is one of the cheaper repairs, so it's usually worth it unless the machine is very old or has other problems (noisy bearings, leaks, worn door seal).

Separately, it's good practice to press the "T" test button on your RCD every few months to check it still trips properly.
